17.0.0.en: The great whore: a reference to Babylon, the kingdom of evil, and fornication here is a figure for turning away from God and betraying Him by worshiping the world and Satan.

17.0.1.en: That sitteth upon many waters: an emphasis that Babylon is what is meant here, since it lies on the great river Euphrates (Jer 51:13), and like the words of the Psalm, "By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down" (Ps 137:1). The spiritual meaning will be interpreted in (v. 15). One of the seven angels who carried the bowls of God's wrath spoke to St. John, calling him to see the end and judgment of the kingdom of evil and all its followers, who are symbolized by the many waters, and the detailed discussion of this will come in (v. 15).

17.1.0.en: The kings of the earth: all the leaders and authorities who contributed to, and called their peoples, directly or indirectly, to leave God and His worship.

17.1.1.en: In a new description of "Babylon," the angel describes her as the adulterous woman who seduced many peoples to spiritual fornication and used every possible means of enticement, so that most of the inhabitants of the earth stagger and fall into evil and blasphemy like drunkards who have lost consciousness and will.

17.2.0.en: Into the wilderness: a reference to the spiritual poverty and barrenness in which the kingdom of evil lives. Scarlet: a reference to the bloodiness and ferocity of Satan.

17.2.1.en: Full of names of blasphemy: that is, blasphemy against God, either by attributing God's attributes to himself or by mocking and ridiculing God and His attributes.

17.2.2.en: The angel took St. John to a new scene in his vision, "he carried me away in the spirit," and he saw a desolate, frightening wilderness, and he saw the kingdom of evil (the woman Babylon) sitting upon the secret of her strength and support, who is Satan, who carries his kingdom, declaring his ferocity through his bloody color and his hatred of God through his blasphemy and his insolence against His holy name.

17.2.3.en: Seven heads and ten horns: this was explained before in (ch. 12:3, ch. 13:1), and it points to the multitude of his thoughts and their strength.

17.3.0.en: Purple: a red color worn by kings in ancient times, and it is like the robe that the Roman soldiers put on the Lord Christ in mockery of Him.

17.3.2.en: In arrogance and pride, Babylon the harlot took on the appearance of kings to proclaim her greatness and authority, so she dresses like them and boasts of her scarlet color because she shed the blood of many saints and drank of their blood, and adorned herself with the vices and sins that her followers desired, such as gold, pearls and precious stones, and she held in her hand a cup of the wine of her pleasure, by which she is refreshed and delights and becomes drunk. And pointing to the intensity of her evil, God declares to us that the content of this cup is fornication and the abominations from which she gives the nations and peoples to drink, and for this it is called "the wine of her fornication" (v. 2). It is also noted that the description of Babylon in this form agrees exactly with her description as given by Jeremiah in (Jer 51:7).

17.4.0.en: Mystery: that is, the name Babylon here is a symbol, and the discussion is not about the real city of Babylon.

17.4.1.en: Mother of harlots: the origin of all evil and immorality.

17.4.2.en: The impudence and boldness of Babylon in her evil reached the point that she was not ashamed of her shameful sin, but boasted of what she commits and advertised herself, with the shamelessness of fornicators in announcing their name and profession to attract others and ensnare them, for she put her name on her forehead. And her description as the origin of all sin, "the mother of harlots," is because she is the caller and instigator of every kind of spiritual fornication and betrayal of the holy name of God and blasphemy against it.

17.5.0.en: To complete the scene, the woman was in a state of drunken intoxication, and the secret of the happiness and intoxication of her drunkenness is that she was satisfied, and is still being satisfied (the kingdom of evil), with the blood of the faithful children of God who rejected her and resisted her, so she raised persecution and torment against them, and they did not submit or surrender but gave their lives even to death, and therefore their name became great, for they were called "the martyrs of Jesus."

17.5.1.en: And when I saw her, I wondered with great admiration: that is, I was bewildered and found no explanation, and this wonder is considered an introduction to what the angel will make clear to John in the coming verses.

17.5.2.en: In the Law of Moses, the priest in ancient times used to put on his forehead a small plate on which was written "Holiness to the LORD," that is, set apart for the service of God; this was a clear declaration of his identity and belonging. Likewise the wicked put their evil name on their foreheads, to declare also their belonging to the satanic kingdom of Babylon, and many people do not know what they are putting on their foreheads, "set apart for the Lord, or living in Babylon..." Have you settled your matter, my brother, and do you know what title you are wearing and to which kingdom you belong ...?!

17.6.s.en: (2) The interpretation of the preceding vision

17.6.0.en: St. John's wonder at the preceding scene carried more distress than wonder, at God's allowing the woman (Babylon) to delight in and be drunk with the blood of the martyrs, the children of God. So the angel's words to him, "Wherefore didst thou marvel?" came as an introduction to revealing the mystery he was about to declare to St. John.

17.6.1.en: The beast that thou sawest: it is the beast from the sea mentioned in (Rev 13:1-3), which is one of the forms of Satan.

17.6.2.en: Was, and is not: a clear reference to the shrinking of the authority of Satan and his kingdom.

17.6.3.en: Shall ascend out of the bottomless pit, and go into perdition: that is, on the day of the Lord's great judgment he will be moved from the place where the wicked wait to eternal perdition in the abyss forever.

17.6.4.en: The general meaning is that the beast carrying the woman is none other than Satan, who had authority over man, but by the crucifixion of Christ and His redemption of all mankind, this Satan was driven back, as the Lord Christ said to His disciples, "I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven. Behold, I give unto you power) "... (Lk 10:17-19), like the words of the Apostle Paul, "And having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it" (Col 2:

17.6.5.en: 14-15.) (It appears from this verse that Satan dwells in hell and continues to fight mankind within the limits that God permits him, until he is cast with all his armies into eternal torment.

17.6.6.en: They that dwell on the earth shall wonder: that is, his followers who bear his mark and sign.

17.6.7.en: Whose names were not written .. in the book of life: that is, there is no deliverance through him, and it is the natural result for whoever follows him.

17.6.8.en: The angel adds in his speech to what preceded that the followers of Satan or the Antichrist will be seized with amazement and regret over the one in whom they put their hope to no use or profit, for their fate has become clear: it is perdition and the loss of the inheritance of the Kingdom, "the book of life."

17.6.9.en: Was, and is not: the wicked realize that the authority of Satan, with which he used to fight the children of God in the world, has ended.

17.6.10.en: And yet is: although Satan exists in eternal torment, he is unable to do anything.

17.7.0.en: "Here is the mind which hath wisdom" is a parenthetical sentence whose purpose is to urge the reader or listener to concentrate on what is coming.

17.7.1.en: The seven heads .. seven mountains: many interpreters held that the scene here is a figure for Rome in its harsh persecution of Christianity, since Rome is in fact built on seven hills. On which the woman sitteth: that is, she exercised her authority and persecution through this city.

17.8.0.en: Seven kings: many interpreters have labored to say who these seven are, but in keeping with the symbols of the whole book, we see that the number seven here signifies the perfection of the days of the kingdom of evil and Satan throughout history, without being bound to a specific time.

17.8.1.en: Five are fallen: that is, most of them have gone and their days have passed.

17.8.2.en: And one is: that is, at the time this book was written.

17.8.3.en: And the other is not yet come: a prophecy of the coming of a final kingdom of evil before the end of days.

17.8.4.en: In this verse the vision shows us the succession of the kingdoms of evil to the end of days, for the first five kingdoms are those that opposed God and His people with their idols and wars, and they are the kingdoms of:

17.8.5.en: 1- Egypt, which enslaved the people of God.

17.8.6.en: 2- Assyria, which lifted up its eyes against the Holy One of Israel (Isa 37:23).

17.8.7.en: 3- Babylon, which subdued the whole earth (Jer 50:23).

17.8.9.en: 5- Greece, the last pagan error, which defiled Jerusalem and which the Maccabees resisted.

17.8.10.en: As for the kingdom existing at the time the book was written, it is the Roman kingdom, the sixth, which made Christianity taste the worst kinds of torture and cruelty .. And there remains a final kingdom, the kingdom of the Antichrist, of whom the angel indicates that he must continue a short space, that is, his kingdom and his wars will continue for a short period of time.

17.9.0.en: The beast that was: that is, Satan (v. 8). Is the eighth: that is, the last of all evil ...

17.9.1.en: It is clear that the kingdoms are seven and not eight, but the declaration that Satan is the eighth means Satan's domination of all the preceding kingdoms, as if all of them bore his mark, and to show that there is no eighth kingdom the angel declares that his spirit (Satan) is at work and active in the seven kingdoms. And in an ending reassuring to the children of God and in a plain declaration, the angel confirms for the second time, to us and to St. John, the final fate of Satan, which is eternal perdition.

17.10.0.en: In an interpretation of the scene of the ten horns (v. 3), the angel makes clear in his speech that it is a symbol of ten kingdoms or ten kings (heads of nations) to whom Satan gives authority, but in their evil they are not as strong as the preceding kingdoms, since they receive authority "one hour," that is, a small authority, although they will devote all their power, thought and authority to the service of Satan.

17.11.0.en: These authorities or kingdoms or governments declare their clear defiance of the Lord Jesus, "the slain Lamb," so they fight Him and resist the authority of His Kingdom over the hearts of men ..., and the angel declares to us the final result of this war, which is the defeat of Satan and all his followers, and the proclamation of the victory of Christ, King of kings and Lord of lords, who will lead in the procession of His triumph all His chosen children, those called and those who believe in His name (2 Cor 2:14).

17.11.1.en: I thank You, my God, that You announce to us our victory in Your blessed name, so that our confidence in our salvation through You is renewed, and our triumph over Satan by the power of Your blessed name and the sign of Your life-giving Cross. I thank You and ask You, my Savior, to complete Your work in me to the end, so that I may not be disturbed by the wars of Satan, and may complete my striving in peace because You are with me.

17.12.0.en: The waters which thou sawest: they are the same waters he mentioned in (v. 1), but here he will explain them.

17.12.1.en: The angel brings St. John back to the beginning of the scene he saw in this chapter and explains to him some of its symbols. The woman (Babylon) was sitting, that is, she controls and rules with her evil the peoples of the world of every race and language.

17.13.0.en: The events of these two verses came in a way none of us expects; for the woman was sitting upon the beast, that is, he was serving her and devoting his power to her ... But let us see what happens! Satan turned against his own kingdom, and there came anger, destruction and killing, and Satan himself began to burn his kingdom and his followers, pointing to the nearness of his end and his final disappearance, for any kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation (Lk 11:17). And before St. John asks how this happens?...! the angel intervenes and reveals to us the secret of what happened, which is that "God hath put in their hearts," that is, this is God's command and His effective will even over the kingdom of evil with all its powers and systems, for the first counsel and the last word belong to Him alone, however patient and longsuffering He is toward the kingdom of evil. And give their kingdom unto the beast, until the words of God shall be fulfilled: that is, all the authorities and powers and kingdoms gave all their strength and resources to the service of Satan to destroy Babylon, the kingdom of evil. To clarify the idea with examples that bring home to our minds how this happens, we say that God often used some kingdoms of evil to take vengeance on wicked kingdoms that preceded them: the Greeks came against the Persians and the Assyrians, and the Romans came against the Greeks, and so the kingdoms of evil (the beast) rose against one another (Babylon) until they destroyed her and all her authority.

17.14.0.en: And the woman which thou sawest: that is, the woman who is the subject of the discussion in the whole chapter, who sat upon the beast and upon the many waters (v. 1). At the end of the chapter the angel sums up for us the character of the woman, saying that she is "that great city," that is, the capital of evil in different ages: once (Babylon), which humbled the people of God in ancient times; another time Rome, which made the Christians taste the severest degrees of torment; and a third time, the forces of evil and atheism in the contemporary world; and at every time most of the kings and rulers of the earth submitted to her and followed what she commanded them.

17.14.1.en: My God, You leave evil to rage against Your children from time to time, and we wonder, why, Lord, are they increased that trouble us!?! But we thank You, my God, that You announce to us and teach us that all this is only for a time, and we must trust in Your wisdom and Your ordering of the times. What You announce to us now brings rest to our souls and shows us all the more the folly of Satan, who has become without wisdom and without authority over his actions, for in the end he finishes himself by himself, like a madman, a fool who thought himself wise..!!! Let us praise Your holy name and thank Your exalted wisdom now and at all times .. Amen.

17.14.2.en: The destruction of Babylon: introduction: after the previous chapter highlighted how evil was divided against itself, and pointed to the collapse of its kingdom (Babylon), this chapter portrays for us a detailed picture of the fall of Babylon, the reason for her fall, and the weeping of the wicked over her. We also find God's clear call to His children to come out of her, lest the final plagues fall upon them.

18.0.s.en: (1) The proclamation of the first angel

18.0.0.en: And after these things: that is, the preceding vision of the beast and the harlot (ch. 17). The earth was lightened with his glory: a figure for the power, the greatness of authority and the majesty of this angel.

18.0.1.en: In a scene considered a continuation of what John saw in the preceding chapter, here he saw another mighty angel coming down from heaven, making a proclamation long awaited by the faithful children of God, and because of the power of this angel his descent from heaven was accompanied by a great light that lit up the whole earth.

18.1.1.en: The angel proclaimed with a loud voice (a cry) the subject of the message he carries to all the inhabitants of the earth, which is the fall of the kingdom of evil (Babylon), and he repeated the word "fallen" to indicate her final fall, with no rising again or return of her authority, and he adds that she has become a prison for all the demons and unclean spirits and also every unclean bird.

18.1.2.en: An unclean bird: there were kinds of birds that God forbade the Jewish people to eat in the Law, such as birds of prey, and they were hated birds among the people ... But the meaning here is another description of the demons, besides his first description of them as unclean spirits.

18.2.0.en: This verse makes clear to us the reasons for the fall of Babylon and her just judgment, for she:

18.2.1.en: (1) Made all her followers drunk by offering various desires (the wine of her fornication), so these services and desires were the cause of their fornication (that is, turning away from God.) (2) And as she destroyed nations and peoples, so she also brought down many kings and rulers by various tricks to ensure her dominion over the whole world.

18.2.2.en: (3) By enticements and material gains she was able to control the merchants of the earth (the economic powers), so that they worship money and its power instead of God.

18.2.3.en: Very comforting, Lord, is the meditation on the judgments of Your justice, for You announce to us how the kingdom of evil ends and becomes a dwelling and a prison for Satan and his unclean spirits; but I, my God, look with longing to the other dwelling, where You are there, a shining light and warmth and tenderness and rest without end, and until we meet You there and enjoy the sight of You, I pray to You and ask You to complete for us the way of our salvation and to rescue us from the earthly (Babylon) with all her evil desires and pleasures.

18.3.s.en: (2) The warning of the second angel

18.3.0.en: St. John heard a second voice, also from heaven, and this voice carried a warning from God to His people, calling them to come out of Babylon before He brings His punishment upon her; and the spiritual meaning here is that God calls us and urges us to depart from evil finally, for spiritual Babylon is not a particular place but a state present now everywhere, but the faithful children of God must flee from every form of evil.

18.3.1.en: That ye be not partakers of her sins: this is the reason for God's call to us to withdraw from evil, because it is impossible for a person to live inside the kingdom of evil without being affected by it or by its enticements ... This also reminds us of the angel's call to Lot to flee from Sodom and Gomorrah (wicked Babylon) before their destruction and burning (Gen 19).

18.4.0.en: Her sins have reached unto heaven: a pictorial expression indicating the severity of her evil. As the inspired text also describes that the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah had reached the Lord (Gen 18:20). God hath remembered her iniquities: this does not of course mean that God had forgotten, but that the time of punishment and judgment has come.

18.5.0.en: After God commanded His people and those who love Him to come out of Babylon and withdraw from evil, His direct command to repay her comes. This command is of course directed to God's servants, the angels who carry out His will, and we notice about God's repayment that it is:

18.5.1.en: (1) Just: "Reward her even as she rewarded you," that is, as she tormented the children of God with many torments.

18.5.2.en: (2) Doubled: "Double unto her double," that is, she will suffer as no one has ever imagined or thought, and as she mixed desires and enticements in the cup of her fornication, it is now her turn to drink from the same cup, but here she drinks a doubled mixture of the wrath of God.

18.6.0.en: She hath glorified herself: the characteristic of Satan and of evil is pride and boasting.

18.6.1.en: Lived deliciously: in earthly and sensual pleasures and sinful, passing desires.

18.6.2.en: I am no widow: I am not in want or need and I will not see old age or an end.

18.6.3.en: In pride and haughtiness Babylon looked upon the glories of her evil, and in stupidity and pride she did not suppose for a moment that all this has a certain end, so the voice of her boasting rose and she declared that she is a queen and a young woman living in luxury and there is no passing away of her glory or her false happiness..; and for this God's sentence came that she should pay the price of her stubbornness and unrepentance, so in proportion to her fornication and evil she will also receive her portion of torment and sorrow and wailing and gnashing of teeth.

18.7.0.en: In a proclamation that reassures the children of God by the power of their heavenly Father and the might of His right hand, saving to His children and destroying to those who oppose and resist Him, he tells us how the day of God's vengeance will be.

18.7.1.en: In one day: that is, the plagues come in succession and with speed, and the day is a reference to the day of the last judgment; and these plagues begin with death, that is, the proclamation of the destruction of all her inhabitants and her kings, and mourning and famine are two punishments that correspond to the glory and luxury (v. 7) by which she deceived and seduced her children, and the fire that burns her is the punishment of her fornication that awaits her, as the Law commanded in the punishment of fornicators (Lev 20:14, 21:9). The meaning intended by death here may be the end of the whole world, and consequently her eternal fate (Babylon's) is perpetual mourning and a hunger for the rest that the wicked do not find, and then burning with a fire that is not quenched.

18.7.2.en: Beloved, do not be amazed if you see the boasting and prosperity of the wicked and the success of their ways ... and be assured that they have a short time, but after this they pay the price of their luxury. So reject evil and all its desires strongly, for in proportion as you flee from (Babylon), as Joseph fled from the offers and enticements of sin, we will have deliverance in the name of our Savior Christ and the inheritance of His eternal throne.

18.8.s.en: (3) The grief and lament of her followers

18.8.0.en: The kings of the earth: an expression that points to the proud and haughty, to whom evil gave authority and worldly influence (leaders or politicians). Lived deliciously with her: they satisfied their evil desires through her (the kingdom of evil). Everyone who had any standing stood, and their hopes were disappointed and ended as they saw their kingdom collapsing before their eyes into destruction, and her eternal judgment and harsh torment had begun. And because her torment and judgment is a declaration of their own end and judgment too, their weeping, mourning and crying came not only over the city but also over themselves, since their fate had become before them, and for this they uttered the expression "Alas, alas," to declare their anguish at what has come upon her and their terror at what awaits them.

18.8.1.en: Standing afar off: it may be a picture showing a time difference between the judgment of the kingdom of evil (Babylon) and then of her followers (the kings of the earth), and it is an expression that points to the severest kinds of torment, for how cruel it is for a person to see the judgment and torment of another while knowing that he is seeing what will happen to himself also.

18.9.0.en: The second kind are "the merchants of the earth"; if the first kind were attracted by authority, influence and rule, there are also those whom love of money and gold enslaved, and whom the world attracted with its business and deals, and all their hope was in increasing their money and leaving it as an inheritance to their children. What they weep over now is their discovery of the deception into which they fell and that all they did is worthless, "no man buyeth their merchandise any more," and of course their mourning is also over the torment and judgment that await them, which have become present before them, as was the feeling of the kings of the earth.

18.10.2.en: Scarlet: red cloth darker than purple.

18.10.3.en: Thyine wood: fragrant wood from the citron tree found in North Africa.

18.10.4.en: Marble: one of the finest kinds of marble.

18.10.8.en: These two verses make clear the kinds of trade of these merchants, which included everything, beginning with precious riches (such as gold, silver, pearls and precious stone), then the most splendid garments (purple, scarlet and fine linen), followed by what ordinary people need in their homes (ivory, wood and iron) to furnish their houses, and what everyone needs for eating (such as oil, wheat and the flesh of cattle), then the end was with the worst kind of trade, which is trade in people themselves and their bodies (the trade of fornication...). The purpose of presenting all these kinds of goods to the merchants is to expose what is happening in the world now, for the merchants, the followers of (Babylon) and the kingdom of evil, made it lawful to trade in everything, the lawful and the unlawful, and the purpose was to exploit people to make their gain and to entice them constantly to buy, so that man remains all his life a captive of his desires and ambitions and material needs; on the one hand the wealth of the merchants of evil increases, and on the other hand people forget the salvation of their souls in their rush to buy.

18.10.9.en: In a more spiritual way it can be said that the merchants here are the demons and the goods are the enticements and desires, and their variety means that Satan offers each person what entices him, whether it is clear evil (people's bodies) or hidden sins that he persuades people they badly need (such as adornment, clothing and desires for food), so he ties all people with threads whose end is in his hand, and controls the whole world by this trade of his.

18.10.10.en: I thank You, my God, that You expose to me the plans of the merchants of evil. So understand, O my soul, and be chaste, and do not ask for more than you need, and be content with what you have, lest you lose your authority over yourself and give it to Satan, for in the end he will give you to taste nothing but the husks of the swine, that is, humiliation and misery.

18.11.2.en: The words here in their direct meaning refer to (Babylon), who lost everything, and also her merchants, who lost their trade with her burning.

18.11.3.en: As for the spiritual meaning, it can be applied to every soul that went after its desires and thereby lost the fruit of the Holy Spirit expected of it, and the radiant Christ departed from it and it will not find Him afterward, since it left Him first, so He left it finally and deprived it of its eternal inheritance.

18.12.0.en: These two verses correspond in their meaning and picture with what is said in (vv. 9, 10) about the kings of the earth, for the merchants also shared in the mourning, weeping, lamentation and great fear, not only over the passing splendor of the kingdom of evil but also over the torment that awaits them.

18.12.1.en: Clothed in fine linen .. arrayed in fine linen: that is, she who once had splendor. Shipmasters: the captains of ships.

18.12.2.en: Sailors: those who keep the sea charts and guide the ships.

18.13.0.en: The words here are about the third group (the shipmasters and sailors at sea) after the kings of the earth and her merchants, and this third group signifies the middlemen of evil, that is, those who transport it from one place to another and promote it or import strange sins and re-export them, and the Lord Christ Himself cursed them when He said, "Woe unto that man by whom the offence cometh!" (Mt 18:7). They too cried out when they saw the collapse and burning of the city of their harbor, and they never believed in her end, for they thought she was great and above all destruction.

18.14.0.en: Dust on their heads: an ancient custom of the Eastern peoples to show intense grief.

18.14.1.en: The shipmasters and sailors repeated almost what the kings and merchants had repeated before, as their hopes collapsed and were ruined with the end and destruction of Babylon, for after having been the cause of their wealth she has now become desolate before their eyes. And their cry, as we explained before, is their fear of their coming fate.

18.15.0.en: Rejoice: this is a call from the same angel who proclaimed the judgment of Babylon, for he also proclaims the joy of the kingdom of heaven.

18.15.1.en: The angel declares to the heavenly creation and all the martyrs good news, which is the end of Babylon and the beginning of her judgment and the proclamation of divine justice, and the expression that "God hath avenged you on her" is an answer to the question that the holy martyrs asked: "How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood" (Rev 6:10). And so, just as God's mercies gladden heaven and the saints by the acceptance of the penitent, so also His justice in repaying the wicked gladdens all heaven, because it is a victory for the truth and not a gloating over the wicked.

18.16.s.en: (4) The confirmation of the fall of evil (Babylon)

18.16.0.en: A stone like a great millstone: a millstone is a heavy stone used in grinding wheat.

18.16.1.en: After this St. John saw an angel whom he described as "mighty," pointing to the greatness of the work he was about to do, for he took up a large round stone and cast it into the sea, so that it sank quickly because of its great weight, then he declared afterward that what he did with the stone is a representation of what will be done to great Babylon in her strength and weight, that is, her end and her disappearance from the face of the earth forever.

18.17.0.en: In these two verses he confirms the features of the death and final end of the city of evil, making clear the end of everything in it that carries marks of life or joy or movement .. There will be no more in her one who sings with his voice or strikes and plays the instruments of joyful music, such as the harp (the stringed instrument) or the pipe (the wind instrument). And what happened to the makers of entertainment happens also to every industry, even the necessary ones such as preparing the flour that would be used as bread for her, that is, she will lose even necessary food and die.

18.17.1.en: And as her works will end, her entertainment will be quenched, every light in her, and light is usually linked with glory, so her passing away means the passing and end of the glory of the kingdom of evil, of which she boasted for a time .. and likewise there will be no joys in you at all, "the voice of the bridegroom and of the bride."

18.17.2.en: And in the end the angel repeats to us what has been announced many times, that the reason for her destruction is God's just vengeance on her merchants (v. 11), who supplied her with every kind of evil and facilitated the seduction of the whole earth, and likewise her sorcery, which attracted and led astray most of the peoples.

18.18.0.en: This verse adds another reason for the carrying out of God's just punishment and the destruction of Babylon, which is her shedding of the blood of His children the prophets and the saints and all those she killed among the inhabitants of the earth, whether by persecuting them or by seducing them.

18.18.1.en: Truly the end of evil is painful and shameful and there is no escape from it .. Here is the end for everyone who neglected and made light of God's successive warnings .. So we must repent every day, even if with a few words, lest the heedlessness of life take us and (Babylon) with her sorcery and enticements make us fall, so that we sink with her in the sea of the judgment of perdition and lose our eternal life.
